evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Turns the three loop phases into the methods of a `Game` class -- handle_events(), update(dt), render(), run() -- as the architectural skeleton for 20.33 and chapter 21.

`run()` computes `dt = self.clock.tick(60) / 1000` and calls the three phases in order. -- Confirmed -- the shipped bouncing_ball.py:158-164 implements exactly this, and it runs clean for 180 headless frames.

The pause check must live in update(), not only in render(), or objects keep moving invisibly and the game appears to teleport on resume. -- Confirmed -- notebook 20-26 pauses a MiniGame, runs 30 more frames and asserts the position is byte-identical; notebook 20-33 does the same against the real project.

The listing is a skeleton, not a runnable file. -- Confirmed and, unusually, stated outright -- the text lists exactly what it omits (imports, SHIRINA/VYSOTA, SostoyanieIgry, toggle_pause body) and points at 20.33 for the complete version. The honest way to present a fragment.
Chapter 21's space shooter uses the same architecture. -- Confirmed -- space_shooter.py defines `class Game` at line 327 with handle_events (405), update (498), render (545) and run (651).
